The **R<sup>2</sup>D Canon** is the master source document for
Recursively Realized Distinguishability.

The current integrated archive is approximately **2,750 pages** and
contains the four-part formal development of R<sup>2</sup>D together
with a growing series of addenda that extend, test, and refine the
framework.

It is intentionally large.

The Canon is not primarily designed to be read from beginning to end
like a conventional textbook or journal article. It serves a different
purpose: to preserve the complete mathematical and conceptual
architecture of R<sup>2</sup>D in one authoritative source.

## Why the Canon Exists

R<sup>2</sup>D changes the order in which scientific objects and laws
are interpreted. A focused paper on muscle, thermodynamics, quantum
mechanics, gravity, or biology cannot reproduce the entire framework
every time.

The Canon therefore provides the common source beneath those narrower
developments.

It preserves:

- the primitive definitions and mathematical architecture of R<sup>2</sup>D;
- the derivations and logical dependencies connecting those definitions;
- physical mappings and empirical calibrations;
- applications across scientific domains;
- failed routes, qualifications, and unresolved questions;
- and the subsequent addenda through which the framework continues to develop.

The Canon has three primary roles.

### Archive

The Canon preserves the development of R<sup>2</sup>D as completely as
possible at a particular stage of the program.

Formal versions are deposited on Zenodo so that earlier formulations
remain permanently available, citable, and distinguishable from later
developments.

### Authoritative Source

The Canon is the authoritative mathematical source for R<sup>2</sup>D.

The explanatory pages on R2DScience.org are designed to make the
framework easier to navigate, understand, and use. Applications isolate
particular scientific problems. Essays provide interpretation and
commentary.

When a question depends on the formal definitions, assumptions,
derivations, or logical status of an R<sup>2</sup>D claim, the Canon is
the reference document.

### AI Source Corpus

The Canon is also designed to be used by artificial intelligence.

R<sup>2</sup>D introduces a mathematical language that differs from the
physical ontologies normally used in science. An AI given only a short
description will tend to translate that language immediately back into
familiar concepts such as particles, forces, fields, trajectories,
energy, space, or time.

The Canon provides enough of the internal mathematical structure for an
AI to remain inside the R<sup>2</sup>D framework long enough to
interrogate it.

It can therefore be supplied to an LLM as a source corpus and used to:

- reconstruct an R<sup>2</sup>D argument;
- test a proposed implication;
- search for internal contradictions;
- compare R<sup>2</sup>D with an established scientific theory;
- analyze a scientific law or paradox;
- and explore whether a scientific problem changes when its inherited
  physical ontology is removed.

The goal is not for an AI to accept R<sup>2</sup>D.

The goal is to give AI enough of the mathematics to **run it**.

# The Four Parts

## Part I — The Primitive Count Architecture

Part I develops R<sup>2</sup>D before physical units are assigned.

It begins with counting and develops the dimensionless architecture of
boundary, distinguishability, multiplicity, occupancy, occurrence,
possibility, constraint, closure, recursive replacement, and
background.

Its central task is to define the mathematical objects that must exist
before familiar physical quantities are assigned.

## Part II — Thermodynamic Readability

Part II asks what the primitive architecture looks like when both sides
of the recursive relation remain physically readable.

Thermodynamics provides the primary bridge.

Gibbs free energy, chemical activity, entropy, heat, work, mechanical
constraint, molecular motors, and muscle are examined as physical reads
of relations first defined in dimensionless count form.

Muscle is especially important because chemical, thermodynamic, and
mechanical quantities can be measured in the same functioning system
while the scientific object changes across scale.

## Part III — Readability Horizons

Part III asks what happens when the recursive relation is no longer
jointly readable.

It develops recursive recurrence, occupancy statistics, and two
complementary readability limits.

At the **quantum-facing horizon**, recurrence remains readable while
subordinate distinguishability is lost.

At the **gravitational-facing horizon**, distinguishability remains
readable while the relevant enclosing recurrence is lost.

Thermodynamic and biological systems occupy the jointly readable regime
between those limits.

## Part IV — Projection

Part IV asks what physical description is constructed from what remains
readable after joint access to the primitive count relation is lost.

Particles, mass, charge, motion, fields, quantum amplitude, gauge
structure, gravity, spacetime, and cosmology are examined as
boundary-specific physical projections rather than primitive starting
objects.

Part IV also introduces the converse problem of **deprojection**:
whether a familiar physical description can be traced back toward the
more primitive count architecture from which it is read.

# The Addenda

The four Parts establish the core architecture. The **addenda are the
continuing research program**.

Rather than repeatedly rewriting the Canon whenever a new consequence
is developed, an addendum begins from the existing framework and asks
what follows in a more narrowly defined problem.

The addenda currently extend R<sup>2</sup>D across several major
directions, including:

- direct experimental tests of recursive replacement in muscle and
  molecular motors;
- biological scale transitions, probe-frequency-dependent readability,
  protein folding, and biological function;
- the relationship between the jointly readable biological regime and
  the quantum and gravitational readability horizons;
- relativity, reference geometry, mass, free fall, curvature, and the
  Einstein projection;
- gravitational area, horizons, black-hole multiplicity, and boundary
  clocks;
- gravitational radiation and recursive carry;
- and cosmological boundary structure and large-scale gravitational
  projection.

The addenda deliberately distinguish between results that follow
directly from the formal architecture, empirical mappings, physical
calibrations, hypotheses, and more speculative extensions.

They are therefore not a separate theory appended to the Canon.

They are the record of **R<sup>2</sup>D being run against science**.

# A Living Framework, a Fixed Archive

R<sup>2</sup>D continues to develop.

R2DScience.org presents the framework as a navigable and evolving
scientific tool. The integrated Canon provides the complete working
source. Zenodo preserves fixed releases so that the development of the
framework remains permanently traceable.

This separation is intentional:

**The website is the interface.**

**The Canon is the source.**

**Zenodo is the archive.**

And increasingly:

**AI is the instrument used to interrogate it.**
